head: HEAD of claude/fb1-C (the commit adding this file); code head 85a5aba

requirements.what_changed: certify() takes physical_evidence rows and binds them to the content hash (CIR + written text, the same digest a grant carries) computed on every run, granted or not; exact slug@version+hash, or a declared compatible variant carrying this content hash; a changed hash is reported 'invalidated', a row with no hash does not bind. handle_certify reads PhysicalTest rows (measured.content_hash, else the content the append-only certify audit recorded for slug@version at or before completed_at) and audits content_hash + binding on gate.certified/gate.blocked.
requirements.remaining: physical.record (runtime/release.py, not C) should stamp measured['content_hash'] itself and accept a release blocked only on physical evidence -- see needs_from_others; today a Class C release cannot be recorded through physical.record because _load_cir requires a certified release.

requirements.what_changed: Class C unblocks at certify on bound evidence and never on none (was fail-closed forever: physical_test_passed was never supplied).
requirements.remaining: radar.score still refuses to promote any Class C concept ('Class C requires physical testing that does not exist yet', runtime/pipeline.py score handler, not in C's functions); deriving C from CIR features (F-073) not done; the tester workflow deadlock in physical.record (needs_from_others).

requirements.what_changed: certify refuses RISK_CLASS_DOWNGRADE_UNJUSTIFIED when the CIR's class is below the highest class the product has been stored under (Product.risk_class / PatternVersion.cir_json) unless a physical test of this content is bound.

cir/stitches.py: per-primitive calibration status (CONVENTION for basic stitches, UNCALIBRATED for post/bobble/cable/star family and anything unregistered; CALIBRATED only from evidence). Every certificate records primitives{status, uncalibrated, unrestricted}; handle_certify passes calibrated_primitives derived from passed, completed physical tests' stored releases. The readiness unknowns register reports the uncalibrated primitives.
requirements.remaining: The ERROR (UNCALIBRATED_PRIMITIVE refuses unrestricted release without evidence) is staged in research/final_build/waves/fb1_C_strict.patch: it refuses the three texture products (cable/bobble/ribbed), which the pipeline certifies today.

requirements.what_changed: gates/certificate.py::gauge_findings implements GAUGE_OUTSIDE_DECLARED_YARN_BAND (ERROR unless bound physical evidence), GAUGE_WITHOUT_YARN_EVIDENCE (ERROR), non-sc gauge WARNING; the certify wiring, GAUGE_STANDARD stamp, the PDF note rewrite and four tests are staged in research/final_build/waves/fb1_C_strict.patch (git apply --check passes on this head).
requirements.remaining: Not wired on the branch because EVERY product in the repository fails the band -- all 16 flat-catalogue products and nordic-forest (worsted, 16 sc/10cm vs 11-14), market-basket (worsted cotton 18), hexagon-coaster (dk 20 vs 12-17), harbour pullover (worsted 16) -- Launch-0 included. Measured with the patch applied: test_cert_publish_gates 13 failing (nordic forest no longer certifies, so no listing/frames downstream); every pipeline suite that drives catalogue products through the chain is expected to fail the same way. Apply together with the product re-declaration in needs_from_others.

requirements.what_changed: runtime/pipeline.concept_to_cir derives its gauge from the declared yarn via creative.prototype.gauge_for (Concept.yarn_weight, default worsted -> 12.5/13.8) instead of the typed Gauge(16,14).
requirements.remaining: Refusing CIRs whose gauge is typed without yarn/calibration evidence is the staged patch; product modules (vessels, builder, nordic_forest, garments, texture) still type gauges -- not C's files.

requirements.what_changed: publish/eligibility.product_publication + legacy_status: a slug outside products.launch0.launch_scope_slugs() (candidates + each variant's CIR slug) is refused LEGACY_PRE_CALIBRATION unless its stored certificate was granted under the current GAUGE_STANDARD; uncertified is NOT_CERTIFIED. Consumed by release_gates.for_publish, which store.publish refuses on.
requirements.remaining: Until the strict patch lands no certificate carries GAUGE_STANDARD, so no legacy product can clear by re-certification (fail-closed). Pipeline slugs market-basket-trio / hexie-coaster-set are not Launch-0 variant slugs and are therefore treated as legacy.

requirements.what_changed: gates/first_customer.blocking(cir, listing, frames, store) added and called by eligibility.product_publication for every Launch-0 slug on the store.publish path; UNVERIFIABLE/UNRESOLVED block like FAIL; owner_review_required stays true.
requirements.remaining: for_publish passes the stored Listing but not frames (ListingAsset rows are not publish.listing_assets.Frame objects), so 'imagery' reads UNVERIFIABLE on the publish path until frames are persisted in a form check_frame_plan can read. Cost: one call renders both documents (~50 s profiled under load).

requirements.what_changed: launch/readiness catalogue_depth counts only certified versions in launch scope or re-certified under GAUGE_STANDARD (the same legacy_status the publish path uses); legacy is reported separately under legacy_counted_zero with slugs and why; certified_all_including_legacy kept for visibility.
LAUNCH0 scope is now the enforced publication and readiness scope (F-111/F-119), not only a plan.

products/launch0.py childrens-fitted-garments owner_of_the_blocker now names the independent tester route (quality/testers plan, tester_roster gate, quality/physical to record); readiness physical_calibration is blocked_by the new BLOCKED_TESTER ('tester'), never the owner; test scans owner-facing strings (launch0 pipeline plan, every OwnerRequest that can be raised) for an owner-crochet ask.
requirements.remaining: PHYSICAL_SAMPLE (the parked owner ask) is kept as a constant by prior decision and never raised; excluded from the scan explicitly.

requirements.what_changed: Owner-crochet wording replaced; the physical requirement is blocked on the tester route.
requirements.remaining: The F-073 risk matrix (derive risk class from CIR features) is not wired into readiness.

requirements.what_changed: launch/readiness.unknowns(db, requirements) collects: no physical sample (twin uncalibrated), uncalibrated primitives, every intel.etsy_surfaces unknown, Launch-0 ESTIMATED/UNKNOWN price and make-time bases, proxy-only measurements and an unprobed model provider; Readiness.unknowns, to_dict()['unknowns'] and a render() section.

publish/pdf.construction_overview(cir) builds a 'How it goes together' section from cir.components (pieces, counts, construction, resumes, holds) and cir.assembly (every join, method, edges, row/round placement) and prints it before the Instructions heading; None for a one-piece item or copies of one piece with no joins.

intel/childrens.concept_from_cir / parts_in_cir / neck_or_hood_tie_in_cir read applied parts and neck/hood ties off the CIR (materials, piece names/notes, row/op notes, seam notes, designer notes); publish/pdf refuses to render a children's pattern whose own text trips a REFUSE finding; launch0.childrens_view uses the derived parts instead of a hard-coded ().
requirements.remaining: Opening/closure plausibility (head opening vs CYC head circumference, button-band spacing, armhole/leg openings) not implemented; waist-tie free length is not derivable from the CIR and stays None (unknown).

tests_run.note: fallout of the staged patch, see F-112
drain timed out (131 jobs/1200 s) under load avg ~15; the other two failures follow from the incomplete drain; profiled cost of C's additions ~61 s of 1661 s
killed at 1500 s timeout under machine load; not attributable, rerun on a quiet machine

tests_changed.why: asserted physical_calibration.blocked_by == BLOCKED_OWNER; F-071 forbids the owner being the blocker, now BLOCKED_TESTER and asserted absent from blocked_on(owner).
the people set now includes the independent tester alongside owner and integration.
stocked certificates now carry the current GAUGE_STANDARD stamp; an unstamped Build-1 certificate counts zero by requirement (separate test covers that).
declare the yarn weight that holds their gauge (sport for 20 sc, dk for 16 sc); geometry unchanged.
the basket re-declares sport cotton (holds 18 sc) so a sample can be recorded against a certifiable release; subject of those tests is the sample, not the yarn.

tests_changed.test: tests/test_products.py (flagship, two designs), test_garments (every size), test_geometry (round-worked), test_quality (confidence), test_texture (all three, prose shape check)
tests_changed.why: assert via fixtures.clean_but_for_product_truth: granted, or refused only by the product-truth codes -- any other stage's regression still fails; release_hash comparisons use content_hash (always present). Pass on this head and with the strict patch applied.

needs_from_others: PRODUCT RE-DECLARATION (owner of products/*, no FB-1 cluster owns them) before applying research/final_build/waves/fb1_C_strict.patch: declare the weight whose published band holds each typed gauge -- builder.Design yarn 'worsted acrylic'/'worsted' -> 'dk acrylic'/'dk' (16 sc); nordic_forest.py:157 same; texture.py worsted designs -> dk; garments.harbour_pullover 'worsted wool' -> 'dk wool' (16 sc); vessels.build_basket 'worsted cotton' -> 'sport cotton'/'sport' (18 sc); vessels.build_hexagon_coaster 'dk cotton' -> 'sport cotton'/'sport' (20 sc). Twin geometry/yardage do not read the weight, so sizes are unchanged; release hashes change and every product re-certifies (which is what clears legacy quarantine). Alternatively derive gauges via creative.prototype.gauge_for (changes every finished size). Texture products stay refused by UNCALIBRATED_PRIMITIVE until a tester sample.

runtime/release.py::handle_physical_record (unowned): stamp measured['content_hash'] = the certificate content hash of the text the tester worked, accept compatible_variants from the payload, and let _load_cir serve a release whose only blocking findings are physical-evidence ones (PHYSICAL_TEST_REQUIRED, GAUGE_OUTSIDE_DECLARED_YARN_BAND, UNCALIBRATED_PRIMITIVE) -- today Class C cannot be recorded because it can never be certified first.
runtime/pipeline.py score handler (not C's functions): stop refusing Class C promotion outright now that evidence can unblock it (F-081).

Cluster B / integrator: I added the product-scope call inside publish/release_gates.for_publish (not claims_of, which A owns) -- 10 lines appended before the return, plus 'publication_scope' in the verdict. Please keep it when resolving release_gates.py.
Cluster H / integrator: persist the listing frames as publish.listing_assets.Frame-compatible records so first_customer's imagery area can be read on the publish path (today UNVERIFIABLE there).
risks: With the strict patch NOT applied, gauge_findings is a library no runtime path calls (F-112 PARTIAL); applying it without the product re-declaration refuses every catalogue product including Launch-0 and turns many pipeline suites red (measured: test_cert_publish_gates 13 failing).

store.publish for a Launch-0 slug now renders both customer documents via the first-customer gate (~50 s profiled under cProfile on a loaded machine). In SHADOW the gates are computed before the phase refusal, so each shadow store.publish for a Launch-0 slug pays it.

test_cert_wiring and test_shadow timed out on this shared machine (load avg ~15 on 4 cores). A cProfile of the full cert_wiring drain on this branch: 223 jobs in 1661 s, of which this cluster's additions are ~61 s (for_publish product scope 51 s, handle_certify additions <1 s, unknowns 0.04 s). The integrator should rerun them on a quiet machine.

readiness now has blocked_by 'tester' for physical_calibration; runtime/release.py launch.assessed reports blocked_on('owner') and blocked_on('integration') only, so the tester blocker is not in that audit summary (it is in the requirement list).
